claim_a: Plant-based meat was 45% more expensive per kg than animal meat in 2024 (sales-weighted Circana, GLB-09)
claim_b: Meat substitutes had reached price parity in German supermarkets (unweighted shelf sample, GLB-15)
position_taken: Use the sales-weighted premium (+45%) for demand modelling; parity applies to the cheapest private-label items, not to what people actually buy on average
notes: Both can be true: parity at the low end of the shelf, premium in the basket

claim_a: A basket of the cheapest plant-based versions of 12 products was cheaper than the animal basket in most Dutch supermarkets (ProVeg, cited in GLB-10)
claim_b: Plant-based meat averaged 35% more per kg than animal meat in 2024 (Circana, GLB-10)
position_taken: Prefer the sales-weighted average for sizing; note that even where cheap parity options exist, volume fell

topic: Sign of plant-based meat own-price elasticity
claim_a: US scanner studies find negative, elastic demand: -0.84 to -1.55 (GLB-16) and -1.23 for plant-based beef (GLB-03)
claim_b: Dutch store-level scanner study finds a positive own-price elasticity of +1.52 (GLB-21)
position_taken: Use -0.8 to -1.6 as the working range; treat the Dutch positive sign as an artefact of rapid variety and quality growth in 2015 to 2018, as its authors suggest
notes: The Dutch paper is a working paper and its full text was not readable

topic: Is plant-based meat a substitute or complement for meat?
claim_a: Substitute for chicken, turkey, fish (GLB-16); plant-based beef patties substitute for beef patties (GLB-20)
claim_b: Complement for beef and pork (GLB-16); complement for beef, poultry and fish in the Netherlands (GLB-21); cross-price effects small (GLB-24; GLB-26)
position_taken: No firm sign; assume cross-price effects on meat are small and do not assume one-for-one displacement
notes: Relationship varies by cut and format

topic: US plant-based meat household penetration in 2021
claim_a: 19% of households bought plant-based meat in 2021 (GLB-02)
claim_b: The 2025 release gives a 2021 high of 20% (GLB-01)
position_taken: Quote 19 to 20% for the 2021 peak and use the current release (20% to 11%) for the trend because both ends share one method

topic: US natural-channel share of plant-based meat
claim_a: 14% of natural-channel meat dollar sales in 2021 (GLB-02)
position_taken: Do not interpret as a collapse; channel definitions probably changed. Not used in headline findings

topic: Effect of Lidl Germany's price parity
claim_a: Vegan sales rose more than 30% in six months after October 2023 parity (company claim, GLB-13; GLB-14)
claim_b: German plant-based meat market volume rose 6.2% in 2024 and fell 1.7% in 2025 (GLB-09; GLB-08)
position_taken: Price parity by one retailer may mainly shift share between retailers; the national category did not take off

topic: Stated versus revealed demand in Southeast Asia
claim_a: 76% of interested consumers say they would buy plant-based meat at price parity (GLB-48, stated)
claim_b: In the Netherlands, widespread private-label parity coincided with falling plant-based meat volumes and a flat protein split (GLB-10; GLB-12; GLB-08, revealed)
position_taken: Weight revealed evidence; treat stated parity intent as an upper bound for trial, not repeat purchase
notes: Also consistent with the PTC review (GLB-32)

topic: Stated versus revealed demand in China
claim_a: 60.1% of an age and gender matched online sample said they had eaten plant-based meat (GLB-51)
claim_b: Beyond Meat sold under 600 units a month on Tmall and several start-ups closed by 2023 (GLB-50)
position_taken: Stated trial figures from online panels overstate the market; use revealed evidence
notes: Revealed evidence here is journalistic and Low confidence

claim_a: In blind tastings, US consumers favoured a 70% beef and 30% mushroom blend over plant-based alternatives (GLB-30)
claim_b: When told the ingredients, demand for the blend fell (GLB-30); Dutch hybrid products are too small to move the protein split (GLB-12)
position_taken: Hybrids can win on taste but should not be sold on a 'less meat' message alone
notes: Relevant to Vietnamese hybrid formats (for example pork and mushroom fillings)

topic: Thai meat substitute premium over processed meat
claim_b: 736 vs 430 THB per kg, which is 71% more (GLB-53 figures)
position_taken: Report the THB figures and the 71% arithmetic; flag the source's rounding

claim_a: Defaults move vegetarian choice from 2 to 12% to 86 to 89% (GLB-37) and triple plant-based choice (GLB-38)
claim_b: Randomised trials with at least one day of follow-up show a pooled effect of SMD 0.07 across all meat-reduction interventions (GLB-39)
position_taken: Defaults reliably change the meal served; lasting net reduction in meat eaten is not shown. Size institutional channels by meals served, not by diet change
notes: Garnett (GLB-35) found no rebound at other cafeteria mealtimes, which supports some real reduction

claim_a: Alternative proteins 10% of meat by 2025 (GLB-45), USD 140 billion by 2029 (GLB-44), USD 162 billion plant-based by 2030 (GLB-43), 11% of protein by 2035 (GLB-42)
claim_b: Global plant-based meat and seafood retail USD 6.6 billion in 2025, about 0.5% of meat value (GLB-05)
position_taken: Do not use these forecasts as base cases; label Part VI scenarios as exploratory and anchor them on observed ceilings
